title: Largest smooth open of an arbitrary algebraic-space morphism
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Smoothness is tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. An open subspace is a subfunctor whose pullback along every scheme-valued object is an open subscheme. Let $h:X\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces over $B$. There exists a largest open subspace $W_h\subseteq X$ such that $h|_{W_h}:W_h\to Y$ is smooth. Flatness and local finite presentation for algebraic-space morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. If $h$ is locally of finite presentation and $v:Y^\prime\to Y$ is flat, then the largest smooth open of $h^\prime:X\times_YY^\prime\to Y^\prime$ equals $W_h\times_YY^\prime$. Here $X\times_YY^\prime$ is the sheaf fibre product, assigning to each test scheme the pairs of sections with equal images; for schemes it is [def-pc-fibre-product]. No flatness hypothesis on $h$, or finite-presentation hypothesis on $v$, is imposed.

proof.text: Use compatible etale scheme presentation diagrams $ha=bf$, with $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$. Such diagrams cover $X$, and smoothness can be checked on them: apply the presentation criterion to smoothness, which is etale local on source-and-target. More precisely, $f$ is smooth on a neighbourhood of $u\in U$ if and only if $h$ is smooth on a neighbourhood of $a(u)$. For the forward implication choose an open $O\subset U$ containing $u$ with $f|_O$ smooth. Its etale image is an open subspace $I\subset X$, and $O\to I$ is surjective etale. The diagram $O\to V$ over $I\to Y$ is a presentation diagram with surjective source arrow, so $h|_I$ is smooth by the criterion. Conversely, restrict any presentation diagram to the inverse image of a smooth open of $X$; the criterion makes its scheme arrow smooth. Restricting a smooth scheme arrow to an open is allowed by the stated etale locality (open immersions are etale).

source.place: Tag 0DZI proof: etale source locality, expanded through Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target).

proof.text: Let $O_h\subset |X|$ be the union of the underlying opens of all open subspaces $I\subset X$ with $h|_I$ smooth. This is a set of opens in the fixed universe. The inclusion-preserving correspondence between open subsets and open subspaces gives an open subspace $W_h$ with point set $O_h$. To show $h|_{W_h}$ smooth, choose a surjective compatible scheme presentation $U\to W_h$, $V\to Y$. The inverse images of the $I$ cover $U$ by open subschemes; their scheme arrows to $V$ are smooth by the presentation criterion. Scheme source locality makes $U\to V$ smooth, and the criterion makes $W_h\to Y$ smooth. Every smooth open $I$ lies in $W_h$, by inclusion of point sets. This proves maximality and uniqueness. The construction includes the empty union; source locality explicitly allows the empty scheme. By step 1, in every presentation $U\to V$ its smooth point set is exactly the inverse image of $|W_h|$.

source.place: Tag 0DZI proof: union construction using Tag 03ZF; open-subspace correspondence is Tag 03BZ.

proof.text: Now assume $h$ locally of finite presentation and $v:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ flat. Choose surjective etale scheme atlases $V\to Y$, $V^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$, and $U\to X\times_YV$. Their fibre products exist as algebraic spaces and the etale scheme pullbacks are schemes. Put $T=V\times_YV^{\prime}$, $U_T=U\times_VT$. Then $T\to Y^{\prime}$ and $U_T\to X^{\prime}=X\times_YY^{\prime}$ are surjective etale: each factors as composites of base changes of the chosen atlases. Thus $U\to V$ and $U_T\to T$ are compatible scheme presentations. The map $g:T\to V$ is flat: it is the base change of $V^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}\to Y$, whose first arrow is etale and hence smooth and flat, and whose second arrow is flat. Flatness is stable under composition and base change. The map $f:U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation by the chart test applied to $h$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $g$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0DZI proof: translate clause (2) to schemes by compatible etale charts; Tag 03MJ and Tag 0410.

proof.text: Apply the scheme flat-base-change lemma to $f:U\to V$ and $g:T\to V$ from step 3. For every $u_T\in U_T$, $U_T\to T$ is smooth at $u_T$ if and only if $f$ is smooth at its image $u\in U$. Step 1 identifies these conditions respectively with smoothness of $h^{\prime}$ at the image $x^{\prime}\in X^{\prime}$ and of $h$ at the image $x\in X$. Step 2 identifies them with $x^{\prime}\in|W_{h^{\prime}}|$ and $x\in|W_h|$. Since $U_T\to X^{\prime}$ is surjective, this proves $|W_{h^{\prime}}|=p^{-1}(|W_h|)$ for $p:X^{\prime}\to X$. The point calculus identifies the latter subset with the open subspace $X^{\prime}\times_XW_h$, and equality of point sets of open subspaces implies equality of subfunctors. Finally $X^{\prime}\times_XW_h=W_h\times_YY^{\prime}$: on every test scheme both sides are pairs of sections of $W_h$ and $Y^{\prime}$ with equal image in $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0DZI proof, clause (2): Morphisms Tag 02V4 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-smooth), case (2); open equality via Tag 03BZ.

The item statement is unchanged from base (live is still unsplit, there is no repair note and no competing delivery), and it matches 0DZI(2) exactly: h is arbitrary for existence; for the base change, h is lfp and v is flat. Step 1 is the pointwise presentation-diagram equivalence via 03MJ (criterion clauses (1)/(2)), 04R3, 02GP and 03BZ; both directions check out. Step 2 is the union construction with 01V6 (empty cover included) and the point calculus; it gives maximality. In step 3 I verified that T=V×_YV′ is a scheme, that T→Y′ and U_T→X′ are surjective étale (U_T is a base change of U→X×_YV followed by one of T→Y′), that g is flat by étale⇒flat and stability under composition and base change, and that f is lfp by the 0410 chart test. Step 4 applies the new lemma, translates through step 1 on both presentations, gets p⁻¹|W_h| by surjectivity of U_T→X′, then equates subfunctors via the image-of-fibre-product clause. The 'details omitted' of 0DZI are written out (D5). The new node lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change is exactly 02V4(2), self-contained, with stmt_deps equal to its bracketed ids and four kinds of search. Small cases hold (Spec k→Spec k[ε] with a flat g; empty U_T), and non-flat g is the counterexample, so the flatness hypothesis is needed. It duplicates nothing: lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change is case (1) and needs f flat, as do the flat space-locus nodes. It is strictly smaller than the item, and there is no cycle.
